newsitem.title: UK: European stocks seen up after Asia, U.S. bounce.
newsitem.headline: European stocks seen up after Asia, U.S. bounce.

text.p: European stocks were seen opening steady to firmer on Monday after Wall Street and key Asian markets rebounded from sharp losses, but the mood was cautious after the shock of Friday's slide.

Traders said a 1.6 percent bounce in the Nikkei-225 index in Tokyo and Wall Street's climb from sharply lower levels by the close on Friday would aid sentiment, as would comments by Bank of England governor Eddie George that markets overreacted on Friday.
Asked whether financial markets had overreacted to Greenspan's comments, George told reporters in Basle: "I think they did initially, but they soon sorted themselves out."
A speech by U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday, when he spoke of "irrational exuberance" in financial markets, sparked the decline in Asian and European stocks.
The remarks raised concerns that Greenspan was pointing to a tightening in U.S. monetary policy.
Wall Street started Friday sharply down, losing 140 points at one point, but recovered a large slice by the close after weaker than expected U.S. jobs growth in November.
In London, The FTSE 100 was seen steady after Wall Street and Asian markets rebounded from Friday's sharp losses.

But traders said sentiment had taken a severe knock on Friday and any gains were likely to be capped, particularly after renewed talk of an early election following the latest outbreak of tensions in the ruling Conservative Party.
The FTSE 100 ended Friday 88.2 points off at 3,963.0.
In early pre-market trade the FTSE was up 7.1 points at 3,970.1.
German shares were expected to start out firmer after Friday's plunge, indicated by sharp gains in pre-bourse electronic trade. The market was seen supported by a stable dollar and higher Bunds.
The IBIS DAX index was up 20.24 points at 2,852.77, some 60 points over the DAX's bourse trade close of 2,791.96 on Friday.
"I am totally bullish. The market had the weekend to digest what happened last week and is in far calmer form," said on Munich dealer.
French stocks were expected to open higher after Friday's 2.26 percent slide, but volume could be limited, with many investors sidelined for the rest of the year, dealers said.
The December futures contract was trading 0.67 percent higher on GLOBEX at 2,225 on Monday morning, up 15 points.
Technical analysts saw a rebound in Paris but warned of pitfalls.

Dutch shares were seen opening firmer as the feeling grew that markets' reactions on Friday were overdone. Wall Street's recovery was seen initially supportive and buyers were expected to emerge today at current lower levels.
Strong Dutch bonds and the steady dollar both indicated an early bounce.
"Looking at Wall Street and the dollar, it looks like the AEX will open around four to five points up," one broker said.
The AEX closed Friday down 12.18 points, or 1.94 percent, at 616.26, battling back from an earlier 38.71 point drop.
Most other European markets were seen moving ahead cautiously after Friday's losses.
